subject: Follow-up: quantifying token buckets & continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared@finstack.com>, Priyanka Shah <priyanka@finstack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:02:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up: quantifying token buckets & continuous batching assumptions

Jared / Priyanka — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can size a clean POC and pricing outline. I captured the numbers you gave on the call, plus a few clarifying questions below.

Recap of stated workload (from your team):
- Typical request payload: ~220 input tokens + ~280 generated tokens (≈500 tokens per call)
- Steady-state concurrent users: ~12 sustained requests/sec (steady qps)
- Peak windows: ~60–80 simultaneous requests during business-hour bursts (1–2x daily peaks)
- Expected monthly volume target: 30–45M tokens (you mentioned a 36M token target as a goal)
- Latency SLO target: p50 < 250–350 ms for interactive flows; p95 acceptable up to 800 ms for non-interactive backfills

Continuous-batching assumptions you wanted considered:
- Short, interactive requests (many small calls per session) so prefix caching + KV reuse should provide substantial savings
- You expect very few long-context requests (most calls are ≤512 total tokens)
- Batch window preference: keep client-perceived latency < 40 ms added by batching. If we can hit ~25–40 ms batching windows and efficient batching, cost/unit improves notably

Budget & pricing target you mentioned on-call:
- Target unit economics: ~$450–$600 per 1M tokens as acceptable for initial deployment, with desire to drive toward ~$350–$420 with optimizations (quantization, larger batching, reserved capacity)

Questions / items I need from you to build a tailored POC + pricing:
1) Confirm the % of requests that are interactive vs asynchronous backfill (ballpark split, e.g., 85/15)
2) Typical TTL for in-app session activity (how long between user actions before session is idle?)
3) Any hard constraints on p95 latency for the interactive flows (we used p50 target today)
4) Example traffic by hour for a typical weekday (CSV or a quick screenshot is fine)

Next steps I propose:
- Connor/Marissa will provision a 2-week POC environment (dedicated slot) and run a synthetic run with your sample traces.
- FinStack provides the traffic CSV and one anonymized sample request/response pair (so we can estimate KV hits).
- We share a draft economic model (redwood_econ_template.xlsx attached) with base unit costs and sensitivity to batching window, quantization level, and KV cache hit rate.

Attachments: redwood_econ_template.xlsx (unit econ model), poc-setup-checklist.pdf (POC items we need from your side)

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
From: Jared Mills <jared@finstack.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@finstack.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quantifying token buckets & continuous batching assumptions

Connor — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications inline: 

- Interactive vs async split: ~78/22 (interactive is the majority; backfills are nightly batches)
- Session TTL: typically ~45–90s between rapid clicks; we see a tail up to ~5 minutes for longer sessions
- p95 constraint: for primary interactive flows we prefer p95 < 700 ms; internal admin flows can be higher
- Hourly pattern: attached is a 7-day sample CSV (hour_of_day, avg_qps). Peaks are 11:00–14:00 and 17:00–18:30 ET.

On budget: the $450–$600/1M token range is what leadership expects for the POC phase. If you can show 15–20% improvements with batching+cache we can expand committed capacity.

We're OK with a 2-week POC. We will also need an internal summary slide for procurement that shows expected monthly spend at 36M tokens under the POC config.

Attaching: finstack_hourly_qps_sample.csv (sent separately via Drive).

—Jared
Jared Mills
Head of Platform Engineering, FinStack
jared@finstack.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared@finstack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Priyanka Shah <priyanka@finstack.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:46:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quantifying token buckets & continuous batching assumptions

Appreciate that Jared — that split and TTL numbers are super helpful. A few concrete notes so internal and procurement decks align: 

1) Modeling assumptions we'll use for the POC econ sheet:
   - Avg tokens per call: 500 (220 in / 280 out)
   - Steady qps: 12, peak concurrent inflight requests: 80 (we'll simulate the hourly bursts you provided)
   - Batch window options we'll test: 15 ms, 30 ms, 60 ms — we'll report p50/p95 impact and cost per 1M tokens under each
   - KV cache hit scenarios: 0%, 35%, 65% — interactive sessions with 45–90s TTL should give us mid/high cache hit rates

2) Cost sensitivity: we'll calculate delivered $/1M tokens under three routes: hosted on-demand, reserved dedicated (monthly commit), and reclaimed private lanes (if you go that route later). Expect initial POC numbers to be higher than committed pricing; we'll show committed glide path.

3) Data needs (quick): the CSV you mentioned + one representative payload (headers removed) so we can reproduce tokenization distribution. Share that Drive link and I will set up an ingestion job on our side.

Action items:
- FinStack: post Drive link to sample CSV + one anonymized request sample (Jared)
- Redwood: spin up POC stack + run synthetic test and deliver econ sheet + a 45-minute demo of POC results at the end of week 2 (Connors / Marissa)

I'll schedule the end-of-POC review for Thu, Feb 25 at 10:00 AM ET — sending calendar soon.

Connor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: quantifying token buckets & continuous batching assumptions

Forwarding for ops: I'll take point on provisioning the dedicated POC pool and coordinating with infra. Connor — I'm pulling the POC checklist into our runbook and will update the sheet with projected costs for the 3 batching windows you listed. Aisha — can you run the first synthetic pass once infra is up? Expect the following internal timeline: 

- Feb 12: infra ready + ingestion job configured
- Feb 13–18: synthetic runs + incremental tuning (batch window / kv hit instrumentation)
- Feb 19–24: live ingest with FinStack traces + finalize econ model
- Feb 25: 45-min review with FinStack (Connors + Marissa)

I'm attaching the POC checklist and I'll add infra tags in the runbook.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
